title: Release Safeguard Wizard: visuals & quickstart screenshots for variant safety checks
creator: Claire Zhang
description: Create a compact onboarding 'Release Safeguard Wizard' UX flow and a library of product screenshots and doc visuals for rollouts, version pinning, canary and A/B variant setups. Focus on a single progressive wizard that surfaces pre-flight safety checks (latency and error budgets, regression test pass rate, automatic fallback thresholds) and snapshot-able rule previews for audits. Deliverables: Figma screens, high-res PNG/JPEG screenshots (light & dark), a component spec for the policy editor, and screenshot-ready copy for docs/quickstart.
acceptance_criteria: Complete Figma prototype covering: pre-flight check, canary config, A/B split editor, fallback policy editor, summary & confirm screens
Eight screenshot variants exported (light/dark, desktop/mobile, empty-state, failure-state) at 2x and 3x resolutions
Component spec document with spacing, typography, tokens, and accessible color contrast values
Design handoff notes and a short annotated Confluence doc linking to the auto-generated image archive
PM and ENG approvals recorded in comments and at least one follow-up PR link included
tasks: Sketch low-fidelity flows for the wizard (pre-flight -> config -> summary)
Build high-fidelity Figma frames and interactive microcopy
Create component tokens for health indicators, risk badges, and timeline charts
Export screenshots in required sizes and annotate exports for docs team
Sync with ENG on data surface for pre-flight checks and variable naming
Incorporate accessibility contrast checks and keyboard nav notes
Upload assets to Drive and add links to Confluence page
decisions: Use a three-state health indicator (green/amber/red) with numeric percentile and tooltip breakdown
Prefer inline risk explanations rather than modal deep-links to reduce cognitive load during setup
Show a compact timeline chart for canary progression and allow manual pause/rollback from the summary screen
Fallback policy editor will default to 'automatic' with configurable thresholds; explicit opt-in required for 'manual rollback'
